title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Pliny's shared lotus name does not transfer the tree referent to the Egyptian herb
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Pliny XIII.107 explicitly says a marsh herb in Egypt has the same name as a previously described tree. It then assigns the Nile-marsh growth and a ferment-wash-dry-pound-bread chain to the herb; pigs fatten on its waste. Preserve name continuity while changing entity class and operation ownership, rather than treating the repeated caption/name as one material.

source.observed_content: The text says a herb and a previously described tree bear the same name, locates the herb in Egyptian marshes after Nile waters recede, then assigns fermentation of its heads, washing, drying and pounding into bread to inhabitants; pigs fatten from its waste.

design.mechanism: Treat shared naming as a relation distinct from referent identity. The source explicitly moves from the previously described tree's name to a herb of the same name; the herb's habitat/season and the inhabitants' processing operations belong to the herb. The subsequent product is bread, with waste consumed by pigs and a stated fattening result. Do not carry the tree entity into the herb's process merely because the name repeats.
design.unit: Complete retained Pliny XIII.107–110 herb/root account, noting that the prior tree account to which §107 refers is outside this selected unit.
design.observable_consequence: A later caption/name model would need an explicit name-to-referent transition or an attribute/reference instruction that blocks transfer of processing to the prior entity; a repeated name alone is insufficient. The specific source consequence is that the herb's heads, not the absent tree account, enter the bread-making chain and its residue feeds pigs. No target structure or mapping is claimed.
